limits:
A SEPARATE registration on the same gate as the four #1408 controls (controls/codex-skill-sync-remap, -network-detector, -over-bundle, -provenance), per-axis as those are. This one covers the INSTALL boundary added by issue #1670: since `codex/skills/` stopped being a tracked tree, no CI check vouches for the tree an install is handed, so `--install` itself must compare that tree against what the sources generate and refuse on a difference before publishing anything.

WHAT 'FINDING' MEANS HERE: the adapter builds a real tree with the gate's own `--write` from a tiny fixture repo in a tmp dir, then asks the gate to install that tree into a tmp destination. A finding is the install exiting non-zero, printing its own `REFUSING to install` diagnostic, AND leaving no file in the destination; no finding is exit 0 with the whole tree published byte for byte. Anything in between (a partial publish, an exit 0 that copied nothing, an unrelated failure) scores unavailable, because it is not evidence about fidelity in either direction. The bad case alters one bundled script after generation and RECOMPUTES its SHA256SUMS line, asserting first that the altered tree is internally consistent and that the script really differs from its source. Recomputing is the point: a tampered file under a stale manifest is caught by the checksum reader (controls/flow-helpers-install) and says nothing about source parity; an internally consistent tree that still differs from its source can only be seen by comparing against the SOURCE.

THE ANCHOR is the gate at dca1ac6b, the commit before #1670. It has no `--output-root`, so the adapter hands it the same tree the only way it accepts one - as its OUTPUT_ROOT, which is where `codex/skills/` lived - and its `--install` copies the tree without looking. Measured: exit 0 with the altered bytes present in the destination. That is the blindness, reproduced from the control.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. (1) That a BARE `--install` never reads the checkout's tree - it generates privately instead, so there is no altered tree for it to refuse; that property is pytest-covered (tests/test_codex_skill_sync.py). (2) Anything about copies ALREADY installed on a host: installed-versus-source drift is install-drift.sh's question, not this gate's. (3) Authenticity. The comparison is against the sources in the same checkout, so it proves the tree is what THOSE sources generate, not that the checkout is the one the reader thinks it is. (4) Atomicity or pruning of the publish step, which the #1235 tests own.

anchors.why: HISTORICAL, vendored byte-for-byte from dca1ac6b, the last commit in which `--install` copied the checkout's codex/skills/ tree unexamined. MEASURED against the bad case: it exits 0 and the altered script is present in the install destination - the mirror that differs from its source is published, which is exactly what #1670's acceptance says must be refused.
